comparator.name: Rechtsgeleerdheid
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 regulations specify 60 EC shared across six tracks and 120 EC specific to Nederlands Recht, the broad Dutch-law route. The official route page shows the year-by-year sequence. The restricted 5 EC choice and the integrated 10 EC capstone are retained.
components: Includes a computing practical for law students.
Students write a legal publication in the second research skills course.
Restricted choice: one of the two approved introductory courses.
Capstone combining a legal research paper, a written pleading, communication training and a simulated hearing.

routeSelection.basis: The target offers six post-propaedeutic tracks after a common first year. Nederlands Recht is the least specialized route: it continues private, criminal, constitutional and administrative law and adds European and public international law, legal philosophy or sociology, and an integrated student courtroom. This selection follows the target structure and official presentation rather than UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The broad comparative law response, public and international law direction, and law and technology direction each have a coherent basis and feasible schedules. Each pair differs by at least 30 EC, reaching the three-option limit. Tax law, notarial law and legal public administration are recorded as additional official directions.

alternatives.label: Comparative law, politics & society
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines UCR’s full law sequence with politics, sociology, economics, history, research and communication, reflecting the broad Nederlands Recht route without claiming Dutch professional qualification.
alternatives.concept: Study legal institutions, rights, private law and criminal justice in comparative perspective. Politics, sociology and economics help explain how laws develop and how they affect society.
progression: Legal foundations and political theory precede comparative rights and private law, then international law and criminal justice. Constitutional and European Union law cap the sequence. Current offerings and prerequisites pass.

alternatives.label: Public, international & European law
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule concentrates on international and European law, comparative politics, governance, human rights, conflict and historical context.
alternatives.concept: Study public international law, European Union law and constitutional systems. Use political, historical and social research to examine rights, institutions and conflict.
alternatives.distinctness: 6 courses and 45 EC differ in each direction relative to UCR option 1.
progression: Foundations in law and comparative politics precede human rights, international law and European Union law. History and social analysis support later study of constitutional systems and conflict. Current offerings and prerequisites pass.

alternatives.label: Law, technology & governance
alternatives.concept: Study legal institutions alongside AI ethics, data and computing. Explore how technology shapes business and public policy, and use comparative, European and international law to examine governance questions.
alternatives.labelReason: The official IT-recht route grounds the direction. UCR combines substantive law, ethics, computing and public policy without claiming the complete Dutch digital-law specialisation.
alternatives.distinctness: 13 courses and 97.5 EC differ in each direction relative to UCR option 1. 13 courses and 97.5 EC differ in each direction relative to UCR option 2.
progression: Foundations in law, programming and entrepreneurship precede AI ethics, introductory data science and machine learning. Policy analysis and transnational business law complement later European and constitutional law. Current offerings and prerequisites pass.

blocks: Both introduce legal systems and legal reasoning. UCR compares traditions and considers law in society.
Both examine fundamental rights. UCR considers human-rights traditions and international protection, alongside comparative material.
Both address criminal liability and core principles. UCR uses comparative examples and a simulated legal aid clinic; Groningen teaches Dutch criminal doctrine in a cumulative sequence.
Both address sources, international legal subjects, jurisdiction and responsibility.
Both examine constitutional institutions and public power. Groningen focuses on the Dutch constitutional order.
Both study private-law principles. UCR compares property, tort and contract across jurisdictions; Groningen teaches Dutch civil law.
Both examine EU institutions, the EU legal order and the internal market.
Both study commercial law and contractual relationships. UCR focuses on business across borders.
Both consider how incentives and public rules affect economic outcomes. UCR covers public intervention and welfare rather than the full law-and-economics course.

Groningen requires one introductory legal philosophy or legal sociology course. UCR offers related general philosophy and sociology.
Groningen continues the legal foundations sequence and includes a computing practical for law students.
Groningen introduces Dutch administrative law. UCR covers selected administrative topics within broader legal courses.
Groningen studies the Dutch parliament and constitution. UCR political science courses provide related context.
Groningen studies administrative decisions under Dutch law.
Groningen introduces research using legal sources and methods. UCR provides broader empirical research training.
Groningen teaches legal history. UCR history courses primarily cover wider social and political history.
Groningen students write a legal publication. UCR research training uses other disciplinary methods.
The Groningen capstone integrates legal writing and a hearing. UCR’s optional independent research is a separate opportunity.

notes.text: Groningen teaches Dutch law through a sequence in civil, criminal, constitutional and administrative law, with dedicated legal research and a courtroom capstone. UCR offers comparative, European and international law alongside other disciplines. These options do not establish eligibility for regulated Dutch legal professions.

audience.programmeDescription: Rechtsgeleerdheid at the University of Groningen starts with a common year of legal study. The Nederlands Recht route develops Dutch law through further doctrine, legal research and a courtroom capstone.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines comparative law with politics, society and economics. Other options emphasise public and international law or the governance of technology.

componentNotes.y1-general-2: Includes a computing practical for law students.
componentNotes.y3-philosophy-sociology: Choose one introductory course in legal philosophy or legal sociology.
componentNotes.y3-court: For this route, complete at least 90 EC, including all first-year courses, and pass both legal research skills courses before registration.

cellNotes.text: UCR compares several legal systems. Groningen’s course is part of a sequence in Dutch civil law.
The courses share basic criminal-law principles. Groningen teaches Dutch criminal law in three stages.
